params.xref_id: An external cross-reference CURIE (prefix:local), e.g. OMIM/MONDO/ICD-10, to resolve back to the Orphanet term(s) that map to it.
params.offset: Rows to skip for forward paging (default 0).

name: orphanet_search_diseases
description: Full-text search over Orphanet disease names, synonyms, and definitions (FTS, relevance-ranked); returns {orpha_code, name, score} plus top-level pagination fields {total, returned, limit, offset, truncated, next_offset}. When truncated, next_commands carries a forward-page step. Obsolete terms are excluded unless include_obsolete=true. Signature: search_diseases(query, limit=, offset=, include_obsolete=, response_mode=).

params.query: A disease label, synonym, or ORPHAcode (ORPHA:166024 or 166024).
params.offset: Rows to skip for forward paging (default 0).

name: panelapp_compare_panels
description: Diff genes across 2-5 panels server-side: shared genes, genes unique to each panel, and per-panel confidence deltas. Pass concrete-region refs ({panel_id, region}); 'both' is rejected. Cheaper than pulling each panel's full gene list and diffing in context.

params.min_confidence: green | amber | red rank floor; default no filter.
params.response_mode: Verbosity: minimal | compact | standard | full (default compact).

name: panelapp_get_gene_panels
description: Return every panel a gene appears on across regions, sorted by confidence. Query by gene_symbol (required); hgnc_id is an OPTIONAL result filter, not a standalone query.

params.gene_symbol: Approved gene symbol (e.g. PKD1). Required: PanelApp queries by symbol.
params.hgnc_id: HGNC CURIE (e.g. HGNC:1100). OPTIONAL filter over the hits -- it cannot stand alone as a query; pass gene_symbol.
params.min_confidence: green | amber | red rank floor; default no filter.
params.response_mode: Verbosity: minimal | compact | standard | full (default compact).

name: panelapp_get_panel
description: Return one panel's detail plus its entity-count breakdown. region must be a single concrete region ('uk' or 'australia'), not 'both'.

params.panel_id: PanelApp panel id (region-scoped, positive integer, e.g. 285).
params.region: uk (Genomics England) | australia. Panel ids are per-region; not 'both'.
params.response_mode: Verbosity: minimal | compact | standard | full (default compact).

name: panelapp_get_panel_genes
description: Return a panel's entities (genes by default; or region | str | all), filtered by min_confidence (green = green only; amber = amber+green; red = all). region must be concrete; widen response_mode for phenotypes/evidence.

params.panel_id: PanelApp panel id (region-scoped, positive integer, e.g. 285).
params.region: uk (Genomics England) | australia. Panel ids are per-region; not 'both'.
params.min_confidence: green | amber | red rank floor; default no filter.
params.response_mode: Verbosity: minimal | compact | standard | full (default compact).
params.offset: 0-based offset into the result set; prefer truncated.next_cursor.
params.cursor: Opaque page token from a prior truncated.next_cursor; pass it to continue paging (rejected as invalid_input only if malformed).

name: panelapp_get_panelapp_diagnostics
description: Report live backend status: the data mode (live), the upstream PanelApp source URLs (UK + Australia), the in-memory cache TTL, current cache stats, and the RED metrics snapshot (request/error counts, cache hit ratio, tool + per-region upstream duration p50/p95/p99 -- also exported as Prometheus text at GET /metrics). Also echoes server_version and capabilities_version so a warm client can poll this small payload for drift instead of re-fetching full capabilities.

name: panelapp_get_panels_for_genes
description: Batch gene->panel membership for up to 20 gene symbols in one call: per gene, the panel_count, max_confidence_label, and panels it appears on. Unknown symbols are returned in not_found; over-cap input is truncated.

params.gene_symbols: Approved gene symbols (e.g. PKD1); capped at 20 per call.
params.min_confidence: green | amber | red rank floor; default no filter.
params.response_mode: Verbosity: minimal | compact | standard | full (default compact).

name: panelapp_get_server_capabilities
description: Return the PanelApp-Link tool inventory, vocabulary (confidence labels and ranks, entity types, regions), response modes, recommended workflows, error codes, resources, and live data freshness. Compare `capabilities_version` to skip re-fetching when unchanged.

name: panelapp_resolve_gene
description: Resolve free text or an approved symbol to a single rolled-up PanelApp gene. The gene reports its symbol, hgnc id, panel count, regions, and max_confidence_label (the strongest traffic-light label across panels); matches[] always holds exactly that one gene. Pass query (an approved symbol or free text). PanelApp indexes genes by symbol, so an HGNC id is not a lookup key here. region (uk|australia|both, default both) scopes the lookup. Follow up with get_gene_panels to list the panels it appears on.

params.query: Approved gene symbol or free text to resolve to one rolled-up gene (e.g. SCN1A). An HGNC id is not a lookup key here.
params.response_mode: Verbosity: minimal | compact | standard | full (default compact).

name: panelapp_search_panels
description: Search PanelApp panels by name, relevant disorders, or disease group across UK + Australia (region='both' default), deduped and ranked. Use it to find a panel_id, then page via _meta.next_commands.

params.query: Free-text search over panel name, relevant disorders, and disease group (word-prefix match; empty returns all).
params.response_mode: Verbosity: minimal | compact | standard | full (default compact).
params.offset: 0-based offset into the result set; prefer truncated.next_cursor.
params.cursor: Opaque page token from a prior truncated.next_cursor; pass it to continue paging (rejected as invalid_input only if malformed).

name: pgscatalog_get_diagnostics
description: Report runtime state without calling the PGS Catalog: build, upstream request budget (today's usage vs the daily cap), cache hits and tool latency metrics. Signature: get_diagnostics().

name: pgscatalog_get_publication
description: Return one PGS Catalog publication by PGP ID or PubMed ID: citation, title, and the PGS IDs it developed and evaluated. A paper the catalog does not index is not_found. Signature: get_publication(publication).

params.publication: PGP publication ID (PGP000001) or a PubMed ID, as a number or a string (25855707).

name: pgscatalog_get_score
description: Return full metadata of one polygenic score: traits, method and parameters, variant count and genome build, GWAS/training samples with ancestry, the author-set licence, source publication, and download links for the original and harmonized (GRCh37/GRCh38) scoring files. variants_number counts the original file; harmonized files may map fewer. Weights are not inlined, and this server does not compute scores (use the files with the catalog's pgsc_calc). Signature: get_score(pgs_id).

params.pgs_id: PGS Catalog score ID: PGS + 6 digits.

name: pgscatalog_get_score_performance
description: Return the published performance metrics of one score: effect sizes (OR/HR/beta), classification accuracy (AUROC, C-index) and other metrics, each with its evaluation sample set (size, cases/controls, ancestry, cohorts) and covariates, in PPM ID order. publication_id keeps only the records from one paper (e.g. the score's source publication from get_score). The default response_mode=compact gives metrics with short names and lists each evaluation sample set once (samplesets, keyed by the row's sampleset ID); standard/full add the samples inline and the fenced prose. limit=1 just reads `total`. A score with no published metrics returns total 0; an unknown score or publication is not_found. Signature: get_score_performance(pgs_id, publication_id=, response_mode=, limit=, offset=).

params.pgs_id: PGS Catalog score ID: PGS + 6 digits.
params.publication_id: Only records from this PGP publication.
params.response_mode: minimal: record and sampleset IDs with metrics | compact (default): + publication and a page-level samplesets table | standard/full: samples inline (with country) and the fenced phenotype/covariates/comments.
params.offset: Rows to skip; use the previous `next_offset`.

name: pgscatalog_get_server_capabilities
description: Describe this server: PGS Catalog identifiers, limits, data release, terms and licence handling, rate-limit policy and error codes. Signature: get_server_capabilities().

name: pgscatalog_get_trait
description: Return one trait: label, synonyms, categories, description, score counts and the first 50 PGS IDs mapped to it (pgs_ids_truncated says if there are more: page them with search_scores(trait_id)); include_children adds descendant traits and their score IDs. An unknown or retired ID is not_found. Signature: get_trait(trait_id, include_children=).

params.trait_id: Trait ontology ID as the catalog writes it (MONDO_0004989, EFO_0001645, HP_0000822). Get it from resolve_trait; old EFO IDs migrated to MONDO are not_found.
params.include_children: Also list descendant traits and their scores.

name: pgscatalog_resolve_trait
description: Find PGS Catalog traits by name, synonym or current ontology ID (EFO/MONDO/HP) and return each trait's id (the trait_id other tools take) with its categories, match (label, synonym or partial; a hint flags several exact matches), score_count (scores mapped directly) and score_count_with_descendants (direct + descendant traits; what search_scores(include_children=true) returns). Start here: other tools need the catalog's trait_id. Retired IDs are not mapped: search by name. No label or synonym match is not_found, with partial hits as candidates (match: weak). Signature: resolve_trait(query, limit=, offset=).

params.query: Trait name, synonym or ontology ID, e.g. 'type 2 diabetes'.
params.offset: Rows to skip; use the previous `next_offset`.

name: pgscatalog_search_scores
description: List polygenic scores matching ALL given selectors: trait_id (+include_children), publication_id or pmid, pgs_ids; none lists the whole catalog. Rows are in PGS ID order (pgs_ids alone keeps your order). Each row: trait, method, variant count, genome build, ancestry % per stage (gwas/dev/eval; codes in get_server_capabilities.ancestry_legend; no `dev` = no separate development sample reported) and source publication. Rows under the catalog's standard terms omit `license` (stated once as license_default); any other licence is shown on its row verbatim. `total` is exact; page with offset. Signature: search_scores(trait_id=, include_children=, publication_id=, pmid=, pgs_ids=, response_mode=, limit=, offset=).

params.trait_id: Scores mapped to this trait (from resolve_trait).
params.include_children: With trait_id: also scores of descendant traits.
params.publication_id: Scores developed or evaluated in this PGP publication.
params.pmid: Scores developed or evaluated in this PubMed paper.
params.response_mode: minimal: id and name | compact (default): + trait_reported, method, variant count, build, ancestry %, publication | standard/full: + mapped traits, weight type, release date, URL and ancestry sample counts.
params.offset: Rows to skip; use the previous `next_offset`.

name: pubtator_build_topic_literature_map
description: Use this when a user needs a bounded topic-level literature map from a topic query, optionally seeded with PMIDs: returns candidate PMID lanes with bounded summaries. Returns response_size_class. response_mode='compact' is the MCP default for LLM candidate selection; full can be large and is for explicit debug graph inspection. Next: get_publication_passages.

params.query: Topic or research question to build the literature map around.
params.pmids: Optional seed PMIDs (or PMCIDs/DOIs, converted) to anchor the map on.
params.bias_toward: Bias ranking toward these evidence flavors.
params.max_graph_nodes: Maximum nodes in the returned graph.
params.max_graph_edges: Maximum edges in the returned graph.
params.include_authors: Include author lists on graph nodes.
params.include_citations: Include citation edges in the graph.
params.include_pubtator_entities: Attach PubTator entity annotations to nodes.
params.include_related_candidates: Include related-evidence candidates in the result.
params.partial_ok: Return a partial map if a sub-step times out.
params.expand_query_seeds: Seed the map from a query search when no PMIDs are given.

name: pubtator_convert_article_ids
description: Use this when a user provides article identifiers such as PMIDs, PMCIDs, or DOIs and needs normalized candidate PMIDs for research workflows; returns the normalized PMID, PMCID and DOI for each input identifier.

params.ids: Article identifiers (PMIDs, PMCIDs, or DOIs) to normalize to PMIDs.

name: pubtator_diagnostics
description: Use this when a client needs PubTator-Link subsystem status and recovery commands: returns per-subsystem health and suggested recovery commands.

name: pubtator_estimate_publication_context
description: Use this when a user needs to estimate passage count and context size before fetching publication passages; returns estimated passage and character counts plus a recommended passage mode. Do not use this for text retrieval; use get_publication_passages. Next: get_publication_passages.

params.pmids: PMIDs (or PMCIDs/DOIs, converted) to estimate passage count and context size for.
params.sections: Restrict to these BioC section labels (case-insensitive); omit for all. A missing section contributes no passages; a table usually yields a caption and a body passage.
params.mode: Passage selection to estimate under: 'compact_passages' (default), 'full_abstract', 'abstracts', or 'section_text'.
params.full: Estimate under full-text retrieval where available.
params.max_passages_per_pmid: Maximum passages per PMID to assume.
params.include_tables: Count table passages in the estimate.
params.include_references: Count reference-list passages in the estimate.

name: pubtator_find_entity_relations
description: Use this when a user has a PubTator entity ID and needs literature-derived related entities to expand a corpus; returns related PubTator entity IDs with relation types. Do not use this for canonical entity lookup; use search_biomedical_entities. Next: search_literature.

params.entity_id: PubTator entity ID to expand from, e.g. @CHEMICAL_remdesivir (resolve names with search_biomedical_entities first).
params.relation_type: Optional relation type to keep, e.g. 'treat', 'cause', 'associate'; omit for all relation types.
params.target_entity_type: Optional target concept type to keep, e.g. 'Disease' or 'Chemical'; omit for all target types.
params.max_response_chars: Soft character budget for the response body.

name: pubtator_find_related_articles
description: Use this when a user has seed PMIDs and needs similar, cited-by, or reference-linked articles to expand a research corpus; returns related PMIDs with title, journal, year and relation.

params.pmids: Seed PMIDs (or PMCIDs/DOIs, converted) to expand from.

name: pubtator_find_related_evidence_candidates
description: Use this when a user has one PMID and needs related full-text-preferred candidates: returns related candidate PMIDs with bounded summaries. Returns response_size_class. response_mode='compact' is the MCP default for LLM candidate selection; full can be large and is for explicit debug graph inspection. Next: get_publication_passages.

params.pmid: Seed PMID (or PMCID/DOI, converted) to find related evidence candidates for.
params.publication_types: Restrict candidates to these PubMed publication types.

name: pubtator_get_citation
description: Use this when a user provides free-text citations and needs candidate PMIDs for research evidence gathering; returns candidate PMID matches per citation.

params.citations: Free-text citation strings to resolve to candidate PMIDs.

name: pubtator_get_evidence_certainty
description: Use this when a user needs one user-supplied evidence certainty judgment: returns that judgment with its linked passage IDs.

params.review_id: Review the certainty judgment belongs to.
params.certainty_id: Identifier of the stored certainty judgment to fetch.

name: pubtator_get_mesh
description: Use this when a user needs MeSH descriptors and candidate PubMed search terms for a biomedical research query; returns matching MeSH descriptors and suggested PubMed query terms.

params.query: Term to resolve to MeSH descriptors and candidate search terms.
params.exact: Require an exact descriptor match instead of prefix/fuzzy.

name: pubtator_get_neighboring_review_passages
description: Use this when a user needs prepared review passages near a cited stable passage ID for local context expansion; returns the neighboring passages with stable passage IDs and text. This only reads the review index and does not call upstream APIs.

params.review_id: Review index the passage belongs to.
params.passage_id: Anchor passage ID to expand context around.
params.session_id: Optional staged session to scope the lookup to.
params.before: Neighboring passages to include before the anchor.
params.after: Neighboring passages to include after the anchor.
params.same_section: Restrict neighbors to the anchor's section.

name: pubtator_get_pmc_annotations
description: Use this when a user provides PMC IDs and needs raw PubTator full-text BioC annotation export; returns BioC documents with passages and entity annotations. Do not use this for compact grounded answers; use get_publication_passages. Next: get_publication_passages.

params.pmcids: PMC IDs to export raw PubTator full-text BioC annotations for.

name: pubtator_get_publication_annotations
description: Use this when a user provides PubMed IDs and needs raw PubTator BioC annotation export; returns BioC documents with passages and entity annotations. Do not use this for compact grounded answers; use get_publication_passages. Next: get_publication_passages.

params.pmids: PMIDs (or PMCIDs/DOIs, converted) to export raw PubTator BioC annotations for.
params.full: Request full-text annotations where available (else abstract).

name: pubtator_get_publication_citation_graph
description: Use this when a user needs reference or cited-by neighbors for one publication: returns reference and cited-by PMIDs with bounded summaries. Returns response_size_class. response_mode='compact' is the MCP default for LLM candidate selection; full can be large and is for explicit debug graph inspection. Next: get_publication_passages.

params.pmid: PMID (or PMCID/DOI, converted) of the publication whose citation neighbors are wanted.
params.resolve_metadata: Resolve title/author metadata for neighbor PMIDs.
params.resolve_reference_pmids: Resolve DOIs in the reference list back to PMIDs.

name: pubtator_get_publication_metadata
description: Use this when a user needs citation-grade metadata for known PMIDs: returns title, authors, journal, year, DOI and formatted citations per PMID. Do not use this for article text or annotations; use get_publication_passages. Next: get_publication_passages.

params.pmids: PMIDs (or PMCIDs/DOIs, converted) to fetch citation-grade metadata for.

name: pubtator_get_publication_passages
description: Use this when a user needs the text of a PubMed/PMC article by PMID: returns citable passages (title, abstract and, for open-access PMC articles, full text incl. figure captions and tables), not raw BioC. For article-local answering use mode='full_abstract' first (untruncated); sections (FIG, TABLE, RESULTS, ...) selects full text; check coverage_by_pmid. Not for prepared review RAG; use get_review_context_batch.

params.pmids: PMIDs (or PMCIDs/DOIs, converted) to fetch compact citable passages for.
params.sections: Restrict to these BioC section labels (case-insensitive); omit for all. A missing section contributes no passages; a table usually yields a caption and a body passage.
params.full: Prefer full-text passages where the article is open-access.
params.max_chars: Soft total character budget for passages.
params.dry_run: Return a size/coverage estimate without passage text.

name: pubtator_get_research_session_status
description: Use this when a user needs staged candidate, coverage, and preparation status for a research session; returns staged candidate PMIDs, coverage hints and preparation status.

params.session_id: Staged research session to report status for.
params.review_id: Optional review index the session belongs to.

name: pubtator_get_review_audit_trail
description: Use this when a user needs a copy-ready audit block for selected prepared review passage IDs or the latest recorded audit passages without calling upstream APIs; returns that audit block.

params.review_id: Review index to build the audit block for.
params.passage_ids: Specific prepared passage IDs to audit; omit for the latest recorded set.
params.session_id: Optional staged session to scope the audit to.

name: pubtator_get_review_context
description: Use this when a review needs compact citable context from prepared review passages instead of raw BioC export; returns ranked citable passages with stable passage IDs and PMIDs. Use a short keyword query and PMID filters. If zero passages are returned, simplify the query, inspect the review index, or fall back to get_publication_annotations.

params.review_id: Prepared review index to retrieve citable context from.
params.question: Short keyword retrieval question or query.
params.session_id: Optional staged session to scope retrieval to.
params.entity_ids: Restrict retrieval to these PubTator entity IDs.
params.sections: Restrict retrieval to these article sections.
params.max_chars: Soft total character budget for passages.
params.include_diagnostics: Include retrieval diagnostics in the response.
params.allow_truncated_passages: Allow per-passage truncation to fit the char budget.
params.include_resolver_trace: Include the source-resolver trace for auditing.

name: pubtator_get_review_context_batch
description: Use this when a user wants multiple short review retrieval query variants in one call; returns merged citable passages and per-query summaries. Compact (default): query_fair budgeting, next_steps for zero-result queries. Use response_mode="quotes" for short citable snippets or dry_run for diagnostics without passage text.

params.review_id: Prepared review index to retrieve citable context from.
params.queries: Short keyword query variants to retrieve context for in one call.
params.session_id: Optional staged session to scope retrieval to.
params.entity_ids: Restrict retrieval to these PubTator entity IDs.
params.sections: Restrict retrieval to these article sections.
params.max_response_chars: Response character budget: 'auto' (default) or an integer cap.
params.deduplicate_passages: Merge duplicate passages across query variants.
params.include_diagnostics: Include retrieval diagnostics in the response.
params.allow_truncated_passages: Allow per-passage truncation to fit the char budget.
params.dry_run: Return budgeting diagnostics without passage text.
params.include_resolver_trace: Include the source-resolver trace for auditing.

name: pubtator_get_review_index_summary
description: Use this when a user needs one persisted review index summary without loading passage samples; returns its preparation status, source counts and passage counts.

params.review_id: Identifier of the persisted review index to summarize.

name: pubtator_get_review_passages_by_id
description: Use this when a user needs exact prepared review passages by stable passage IDs from prior context packs or audit bundles; returns those passages with text and citation metadata. This only reads the review index and does not call upstream APIs.

params.review_id: Review index the passages belong to.
params.passage_ids: Stable prepared passage IDs to fetch verbatim.
params.session_id: Optional staged session to scope the lookup to.

name: pubtator_get_server_capabilities
description: Use this when a client needs supported tools, transports, formats, and limitations; returns those lists in one capability record. Do not use this for task-specific workflow guidance; use workflow_help. Next: workflow_help.

params.details: Optional capability sections to expand (e.g. 'tools', 'workflow_help'); omit for the default summary.

name: pubtator_get_text_annotation_results
description: Use this when a user has a PubTator text annotation session ID and needs its results; returns the annotated text with entity mentions and IDs once ready. Do not use this for entity lookup from names; use search_biomedical_entities. Next: search_biomedical_entities.

params.session_id: PubTator text-annotation session ID returned by a prior request.

name: pubtator_get_variant_evidence
description: Use this when a user needs source-attributed variant records and literature evidence for a gene and variant; returns source-attributed variant records plus PMID literature evidence. Does not compute clinical classification.

params.gene: HGNC gene symbol the variant sits in.
params.variant: cDNA/HGVS or rsID variant string. Required; use `protein`/`condition` to refine.
params.protein: Protein-level change, e.g. p.Glu23fs, if known.
params.condition: Optional condition/phenotype to scope the evidence.
params.sources: Evidence sources to include; omit for all.
params.max_literature_pmids: Maximum supporting literature PMIDs to attach.
params.include_citations: Attach formatted citations for the supporting PMIDs.

name: pubtator_inspect_review_index
description: Use this when a user needs to inspect indexed PMIDs, sections, passage counts, and failures for a review_id, including source coverage; returns per-source summaries, totals and failures.

params.session_id: Optional staged session to scope the inspection to.
params.pmids: Restrict the inspection to these indexed PMIDs.
params.include_passage_samples: Include a few sample passages per PMID.
params.sample_per_pmid: Sample passages to include per PMID.
params.min_sample_chars: Minimum characters for a sampled passage.
params.limit: Maximum indexed PMIDs to page over.
params.cursor: Opaque pagination cursor from a prior page.

name: pubtator_list_evidence_certainty
description: Use this when a user needs user-supplied evidence certainty judgments for a review; returns the stored judgments for that review.

params.review_id: Review whose stored certainty judgments to list.

name: pubtator_list_research_sessions
description: Use this when a user needs staged research sessions for orientation or one review ID; returns session IDs with review IDs and status.

params.review_id: Optional review index to list sessions for; omit for recent global sessions.
params.limit: Maximum compact session summaries to return.
params.cursor: Opaque cursor returned by a previous session-list page.

name: pubtator_list_review_indexes
description: Use this when a user needs persisted review indexes with preparation status, source counts, passage counts, and approximate storage size; returns one row per index with those fields.

params.offset: Zero-based row offset for pagination.

name: pubtator_preflight_review_sources
description: Use this when a user needs PMID source coverage, PMC fallback availability, and likely full-text versus abstract-only retrieval before indexing review evidence; returns per-PMID source coverage and fallback availability.

params.pmids: PubMed IDs to check source coverage and full-text availability for.

name: pubtator_search_biomedical_entities
description: Use this when a user needs canonical PubTator biomedical entity IDs for genes, diseases, chemicals, species, variants, or cell lines; returns matching entity IDs with names and types.

params.query: Entity name or fragment to resolve, e.g. a gene symbol or disease name.
params.concept: Restrict autocomplete to one PubTator concept type; omit for all types.

name: pubtator_search_guidelines
description: Use this when a user needs guideline, recommendation, consensus, or systematic review papers for a biomedical research question; returns ranked candidate PMIDs with titles. Wraps search_literature with guideline/systematic-review filters and guideline boosting; not an independent guideline database.

params.text: Free-text research question to find guideline, recommendation, consensus, or systematic-review articles for.
params.page: 1-based PubTator3 result page (10 hits each). To continue, use `next_page`/`next_offset` from the previous response.
params.offset: 0-based start position inside `page`; set it from `next_offset`.
params.sections: Restrict the text match to these article sections (lowercase).
params.limit: Max hits to return, at most the rest of `page`.
params.entity_ids: Restrict to articles mentioning these PubTator entity IDs (resolve them first with search_biomedical_entities).

name: pubtator_search_literature
description: Use this when a user needs PubMed biomedical literature search via PubTator3: returns ranked articles (PMID, title, journal, year, citation). Supports flat and section filters and coverage='preflight'. If preflight_error_code is coverage_preflight_internal_error, retryable=false: continue with results or inspect diagnostics.

params.text: Free-text PubMed/PubTator3 query: entity names, gene symbols, HGVS, or a natural-language topic. PubTator3 matches across title, abstract, and, for open-access articles, full text.
params.page: 1-based PubTator3 result page (10 hits each). To continue, use `next_page`/`next_offset` from the previous response.
params.offset: 0-based start position inside `page`; set it from `next_offset`.
params.sort: Sort order. Accepts 'date desc' (newest first), 'score desc' (relevance, default), or '_id desc'. Synonyms such as 'date' or 'relevance' are normalized; PubTator3 sorts descending only.
params.filters: Advanced PubTator3 filter as a JSON object string, e.g. '{"journal":["Nature"]}'. Prefer the flat publication_types / year_min / year_max parameters; do not also set a JSON `type`/`year` key.
params.publication_types: Restrict to these PubMed publication types (case-sensitive, Title-Case), AND-combined with the query.
params.sections: Restrict the text match to these article sections (lowercase, case-sensitive).
params.limit: Max hits to return, at most the rest of `page`; `returned` and `has_more` report what was cut.
params.entity_ids: Restrict to articles mentioning these PubTator entity IDs (resolve them first with search_biomedical_entities), AND-combined with the query.
params.guideline_boost: Boost guideline / systematic-review / consensus articles in ranking.
params.metadata: Metadata enrichment per hit: 'none', 'basic' (default), 'with_abstract' (abstract preview, max 640 chars), or 'full'.

name: pubtator_suggest_corpus
description: Use this when a user needs a compact, review-feeding PMID corpus for a research question: returns candidate PMIDs, roles, coverage hints, metadata, and next commands.

params.question: Research question to assemble a compact candidate PMID corpus for.
params.entity_ids: Optional PubTator entity IDs to anchor the corpus on.
params.must_include_pmids: PMIDs that MUST appear in the returned corpus.
params.prefer_guidelines: Bias selection toward guideline / review articles.
params.include_metadata: Attach per-PMID citation metadata to each candidate.

name: pubtator_workflow_help
description: Use this when a fresh context needs the canonical PubTator-Link research workflow: returns ordered workflow steps with the tool to call at each.

params.task: Workflow to describe; defaults to the canonical 'clinical_genetics_review' pipeline.

name: spliceai_get_server_capabilities
description: Use this first in a cold session; returns the tools, parameters, score glossary, recommended workflows, error codes, and limitations. detail='lean' returns a trimmed doc (tool list + verdicts + error codes + capabilities_version) that omits per-parameter prose already in the tool schemas. Full ~4kB, lean ~1-2kB.

params.detail: full (default, complete doc) or lean (tool list + hash + glossary; params by reference).

name: spliceai_predict_pangolin
description: ONE model only (Pangolin); returns splice gain/loss scores (with positions) for one variant; use predict_splicing for BOTH models with an agreement verdict. Use this for the Pangolin splice gain/loss scores of a single variant. Pangolin is an independent splice model; agreement with SpliceAI strengthens a prediction, disagreement warrants caution. Use predict_splicing to get both models in one call. Returns ~1-3kB. Note: cold calls take 10-30s.

params.variant_id: CHROM-POS-REF-ALT, HGVS, or rsID (HGVS/rsIDs are auto-resolved).
params.response_mode: minimal, compact (default), standard, or full (adds REF/ALT + all-non-zero).
params.cross_build_check: On not_found, probe the other build to detect a build_mismatch.
params.include_hints: Include _meta.next_commands + see_also chaining hints (default true; set false to trim tokens once you know the workflow; also drops the static capabilities_version from _meta).
params.include_see_also: Include _meta.see_also cross-server hints (default true; independent of include_hints -- set false to keep next_commands but drop the 4 cross-server entries).
params.correlation_id: Optional client trace id echoed into _meta.correlation_id (on success and error) so a multi-step workflow is traceable as one unit.

name: spliceai_predict_spliceai
description: ONE model only (SpliceAI); returns acceptor/donor gain/loss delta scores (0-1, with positions) and an optional SpliceAI-10k consequence; use predict_splicing for BOTH models with an agreement verdict. Use this for the SpliceAI delta scores (acceptor/donor gain/loss, each 0-1 with a position) of a single variant, optionally with the SpliceAI-10k consequence prediction (exon skipping / intron retention / frameshift). For a quick raw-vs-masked or single-model question; use predict_splicing to also get Pangolin. Δ>=0.5 is high-confidence. Returns ~1-4kB (full/all larger). Note: cold calls take 10-30s.

params.variant_id: CHROM-POS-REF-ALT, HGVS, or rsID (HGVS/rsIDs are auto-resolved).
params.gene_set: basic (default) or comprehensive GENCODE (much slower; may 503).
params.transcripts: mane (default, MANE Select) or all overlapping transcripts.
params.include_consequence: Include the SAI-10k aberration prediction (exon skipping, etc.).
params.response_mode: minimal, compact (default), standard, or full (adds REF/ALT + exon model).
params.cross_build_check: On not_found, probe the other build to detect a build_mismatch.
params.include_hints: Include _meta.next_commands + see_also chaining hints (default true; set false to trim tokens once you know the workflow; also drops the static capabilities_version from _meta).
params.include_see_also: Include _meta.see_also cross-server hints (default true; independent of include_hints -- set false to keep next_commands but drop the 4 cross-server entries).
params.correlation_id: Optional client trace id echoed into _meta.correlation_id (on success and error) so a multi-step workflow is traceable as one unit.

name: spliceai_predict_splicing
description: BOTH models (SpliceAI + Pangolin) in one call; returns a headline, per-model delta scores, the SpliceAI-10k consequence and an agreement verdict -- the default "what does this variant do to splicing?" answer. Use this as the default one-call answer for "what does this variant do to splicing?". It resolves HGVS/rsIDs, runs SpliceAI and Pangolin (two independent models), includes the SpliceAI-10k consequence prediction, and reports whether the models agree. Read the top-level headline first. For a single model use predict_spliceai / predict_pangolin. Returns ~3-6kB. Note: cold calls take 15-40s (two model calls).

params.variant_id: CHROM-POS-REF-ALT, HGVS, or rsID (HGVS/rsIDs are auto-resolved).
params.gene_set: basic (default) or comprehensive GENCODE (much slower; may 503).
params.transcripts: mane (default, MANE Select) or all overlapping transcripts.
params.response_mode: minimal, compact (default), standard, or full (adds REF/ALT + exon model).
params.cross_build_check: On not_found, probe the other build to detect a build_mismatch.
params.include_hints: Include _meta.next_commands + see_also chaining hints (default true; set false to trim tokens once you know the workflow; also drops the static capabilities_version from _meta).
params.include_see_also: Include _meta.see_also cross-server hints (default true; independent of include_hints -- set false to keep next_commands but drop the 4 cross-server entries).
params.correlation_id: Optional client trace id echoed into _meta.correlation_id (on success and error) so a multi-step workflow is traceable as one unit.

name: spliceai_predict_splicing_batch
description: Score a list of variants in ONE call. The server fans out under its concurrency cap and returns a single envelope with per-variant results (+ per-item errors that do not fail the batch) and a summary. Use this for gene panels instead of N predict_splicing calls. Accepts 1-25 variants (more than max_items=25 returns invalid_input, not a truncated result); each item returns about one compact predict_splicing result, so a full batch is ~25x a single compact response, and _meta echoes items_submitted and max_items.

params.variant_ids: A LIST of 1-25 variants, each CHROM-POS-REF-ALT / HGVS / rsID (HGVS/rsIDs are auto-resolved). Pass an array even for a single variant.
params.genome_build: Reference build applied to every variant. GRCh38 default.
params.gene_set: basic (default) or comprehensive GENCODE (much slower; may 503).
params.transcripts: mane (default, MANE Select) or all overlapping transcripts.
params.response_mode: Per-item verbosity: minimal, compact (default), standard, or full.
params.cross_build_check: On not_found, probe the other build to detect a build mismatch.
params.correlation_id: Optional client trace id echoed into _meta.correlation_id (on success and error) so a multi-step workflow is traceable as one unit.

name: spliceai_resolve_variant
description: Use this when the caller's variant is HGVS, an rsID, or loosely formatted, and you need the canonical CHROM-POS-REF-ALT that the prediction tools require; returns variant_id plus, for HGVS/rsIDs, the gene_symbol and most-severe consequence. Coordinate inputs are normalized locally; HGVS/rsIDs are resolved via Ensembl VEP, which also returns the most-severe consequence and gene symbol. Then call predict_splicing. Returns <1kB. Coordinate inputs are normalized; by default the REF base is also checked against the requested build (one Ensembl lookup) and a ref_warning + ref_validated:false is returned on mismatch (set check_ref=false to skip). HGVS/rsIDs are resolved and validated via Ensembl VEP.

params.variant_id: A variant in any supported form: CHROM-POS-REF-ALT (chr optional; dash/colon/space delimited), transcript or genomic HGVS (e.g. NM_000123.4:c.10A>T or 17:g.43044295G>A), or an rsID (e.g. rs6025).
params.genome_build: Reference build for resolution and scoring. GRCh38 default.
params.check_ref: Validate a coordinate REF against the requested build (one Ensembl lookup) and return a ref_warning on mismatch (default true; set false to skip).
params.include_hints: Include _meta.next_commands (default true; set false to trim tokens).
params.correlation_id: Optional client trace id echoed into _meta.correlation_id (on success and error) so a multi-step workflow is traceable as one unit.

name: spliceai_warmup
description: Pre-warm the SpliceAI + Pangolin Cloud Run containers before a burst so the first real call does not eat the 10-40s cold start; returns per-(model,mask) elapsed_ms, coverage, and stay_warm_estimate_s. Warms the (basic gene_set, chosen mask) path per model; pass mask='both' to warm raw and masked together. Cloud Run scales per-instance, so other param combos or concurrent calls may still cold-start and warmth decays after minutes idle. Returns <1kB.

params.genome_build: Build whose scoring containers to warm. GRCh38 default.
params.mask: Which mask path(s) to warm: raw (default), masked, or both (warms raw and masked per model in one call).

name: strchive_compare_repeat_length
description: Compare an observed repeat count (repeat units, i.e. motif copies) with the ranges STRchive states for one locus and list every range that contains it (overlapping ranges can both match; none may match). Descriptive only, NOT a diagnosis. motif_dependent=true flags loci (e.g. RFC1) where motif identity, not length alone, decides the category. Signature: compare_repeat_length(locus, repeat_count).

params.locus: STRchive locus id (e.g. HD_HTT), gene symbol (e.g. HTT), or the source's disease abbreviation (e.g. SCA3). Case-insensitive. A gene with several loci (ARX, HOXA13), or an abbreviation shared by numbered types (FRA -> FRA2A, FRA7A, ...), returns ambiguous_query with the locus ids to choose from.
params.repeat_count: Observed allele size in repeat units (copies of the motif), not base pairs.

name: strchive_get_diagnostics
description: Report whether the pinned STRchive snapshot is loaded and verified: upstream commit, expected vs actual SHA-256, and locus count. Use it to confirm the data version or diagnose an upstream_unavailable error. Signature: get_diagnostics().

name: strchive_get_locus
description: Get one STRchive tandem-repeat disease locus: benign/intermediate/pathogenic repeat-count ranges exactly as the source states them (closed [min,max] in repeat units; a range the source does not state is null with status not_stated_by_source), pathogenic/benign/unknown motifs and interruptions in gene and reference orientation (all alternative pathogenic motifs, e.g. RFC1), inheritance, evidence level, hg38/hg19/T2T coordinates (BED 0-based half-open; never lifted over), MONDO/OMIM ids and PMIDs. Signature: get_locus(locus, response_mode=).

params.locus: STRchive locus id (e.g. HD_HTT), gene symbol (e.g. HTT), or the source's disease abbreviation (e.g. SCA3). Case-insensitive. A gene with several loci (ARX, HOXA13), or an abbreviation shared by numbered types (FRA -> FRA2A, FRA7A, ...), returns ambiguous_query with the locus ids to choose from.
params.response_mode: Verbosity: minimal (ids + ranges) | compact (default; + motifs, coordinates, ids, references) | standard (+ fenced source prose, HPO ids) | full (+ cross-references, additional literature).

name: strchive_get_server_capabilities
description: Return the strchive-link discovery surface: tools with call signatures, argument aliases, response modes, range/coordinate semantics, error codes, limits, data pin, license and citation. detail='full' adds the usage notes. Signature: get_server_capabilities(detail=).

name: strchive_search_loci
description: Search the STRchive catalog of tandem-repeat (STR) disease loci; returns ranked loci (locus_id, gene, disease, inheritance, evidence level, pathogenic motifs, pathogenic_min) with total/truncated/next_offset. query matches, in rank order: an exact locus id / gene symbol / disease abbreviation; an abbreviation followed by a type number (FRA -> FRA2A, FRA7A, ...); a MONDO:/OMIM:/ORPHA: id; a repeat motif in either orientation (e.g. CAG, AAGGG); words in the disease name, then in source tags (e.g. 'ataxia'), then in the locus HPO phenotype labels. Each row's matched_on says which. Omit query to list every locus. Signature: search_loci(query=, limit=, offset=, response_mode=).

params.query: Gene, locus id, MONDO/OMIM/Orphanet id, motif, or disease words. Omit to list all loci.
params.offset: Rows to skip (default 0).
params.response_mode: Row verbosity: minimal (locus_id, gene, matched_on) | compact (default; + disease, inheritance, evidence, pathogenic motifs, pathogenic_min) | standard (+ all repeat ranges, MONDO/OMIM ids) | full (+ coordinates, tags). No source prose at any mode; use get_locus for notes.

name: stringdb_compute_functional_enrichment
description:
Compute functional enrichment of a protein set; returns enriched GO, KEGG, Reactome and other
STRING terms (category, term, description, p_value, fdr), most significant first.

params.category: Optional term-category filter. When set, only enrichment terms in this STRING category are returned (e.g. 'KEGG' for pathways, 'Process' for GO biological process, 'DISEASES' for disease associations). Omit to return terms across all categories.
params.limit: Maximum number of enrichment terms to return, taken as the most significant (lowest FDR) first. 'total_count' still reports the full number of matching terms, so a smaller limit never hides how many exist.
params.background_string_identifiers: Optional custom background proteome, given as STRING identifiers (e.g. '9606.ENSP00000269305'). MUST be a superset of the query identifiers; STRING rejects a background that omits any query protein.

name: stringdb_compute_ppi_enrichment
description:
Compute protein-protein interaction enrichment of a protein set; returns number_of_edges vs
expected_number_of_edges and the p_value that the set has more interactions than chance.

params.background_string_identifiers: Optional custom background proteome, given as STRING identifiers (e.g. '9606.ENSP00000269305'). MUST be a superset of the query identifiers; STRING rejects a background that omits any query protein.

name: stringdb_get_functional_annotations
description: Get functional annotations for proteins.

name: stringdb_get_interaction_partners
description: Use this to list the top interaction partners (neighbourhood) of each protein, capped at limit per protein; returns preferredName_B, stringId_B and combined score per partner, plus total_count and truncated. Not a pair test: absence from a capped list is not evidence of no interaction; use search_protein_interactions for that.

params.identifiers: Gene symbols (e.g. MAP3K1), UniProt accessions or STRING ids; STRING maps them natively, so no prior identifier conversion is needed
params.limit: Max partners per protein; values above 500 are clamped (limit_clamped_to)

name: stringdb_get_network_image
description: Generate a protein network visualization image as base64 (MCP surface).

params.add_color_nodes: Number of colored nodes to add
params.add_white_nodes: Number of white nodes to add
params.image_format: Image format: PNG, high-res PNG, or SVG
params.hide_node_labels: Hide protein names from the image
params.hide_disconnected_nodes: Hide proteins not connected to any other protein
params.show_query_node_labels: Use submitted names as protein labels

name: stringdb_get_network_link
description:
Get shareable link to STRING webpage for the network.

This endpoint generates a shareable URL that leads to the STRING database
website showing the protein interaction network for the specified proteins.
The link includes all visualization parameters and can be shared with others.

The generated link allows users to:
- View the network interactively on the STRING website
- Access additional features like network customization
- Share the exact network view with collaborators

params.output_format: STRING serialization of the shareable link. All four formats convey the same URL: 'json' returns it structured in 'url'; 'tsv', 'tsv-no-header' and 'xml' return STRING's text in 'formatted' with the URL also extracted into 'url'. (STRING's psi-mi/image/svg link formats are not offered — they carry no link payload.)

name: stringdb_get_protein_homology_best_hits
description: Get the best homology hits between proteins from different species. This endpoint is useful for finding the closest evolutionary relatives of proteins across species boundaries. Returns structured JSON data.

name: stringdb_get_protein_homology_scores
description: Retrieve homology scores for proteins showing sequence similarity to proteins from other species. This endpoint helps identify evolutionarily related proteins across different organisms. Returns structured JSON data.

name: stringdb_resolve_protein_identifiers
description:
Maps common protein names, gene symbols, UniProt IDs, and other identifiers
    to STRING database identifiers. The STRING database uses an intelligent
    mapping system to find the best matching identifier for each input.

    **Supported identifier types:**
    - Gene symbols (e.g., p53, BRCA1, CDK2)
    - UniProt IDs (e.g., P04637, P38398)
    - Ensembl IDs (e.g., ENSP00000269305)
    - RefSeq IDs (e.g., NP_000537)
    - Common protein names

    **Species support:**
    - Humans (9606), Mouse (10090), E. coli (511145), and 2000+ other species
    - If no species is specified, STRING attempts cross-species mapping

params.identifiers: List of protein identifiers to resolve
params.echo_query: Include input identifiers in the output

name: stringdb_search_protein_interactions
description: Use this when asking whether given proteins interact: returns STRING edges (with combined score) among the listed identifiers, e.g. a pair. Absent edge = no interaction at required_score. add_nodes > 0 also adds neighbour proteins.

params.identifiers: Gene symbols (e.g. MAP3K1), UniProt accessions or STRING ids; STRING maps them natively, so no prior identifier conversion is needed
params.add_nodes: Number of additional nodes to add to the network
params.show_query_node_labels: Use submitted names as node labels

name: ucsc_find_blat_alignments
description: Return the genomic alignments of one DNA sequence (BLAT, as UCSC web BLAT), i.e. where the sequence comes from. Hits sorted primary assembly first, then by UCSC score, each with 0-based half-open start/end + 1-based display, strand, identity %, query_coverage %, blocks (several blocks = spliced, e.g. cDNA across exons), alt_or_patch for hg38 alt/fix contigs (primary_total excludes them). `total`/`truncated` are honest. Runs on this deployment's own UCSC gfServer; an assembly that is not deployed answers upstream_unavailable (get_diagnostics -> blat shows what is live). Signature: find_blat_alignments(sequence, assembly=, min_identity=, limit=).

params.sequence: DNA, 20-25,000 bases of A/C/G/T/N (other IUPAC codes refused). Whitespace and one optional FASTA header line are ignored; exactly one sequence per call.
params.assembly: Genome assembly (default hg38). Never lifted over.
params.min_identity: Drop hits below this identity % (default 90, gfClient's default).

name: ucsc_get_diagnostics
description: Report runtime state without calling UCSC: build, upstream request budget (today's usage vs the daily cap), cache hits, tool latency metrics and live BLAT/isPcr availability per assembly (local gfServer status). Signature: get_diagnostics().

name: ucsc_get_reference_sequence
description: Return reference DNA for [start, end) (<= 10,000 bp) on an explicit assembly. Soft-masked: lowercase bases are repeat-masked. strand '-' returns the reverse complement. Signature: get_reference_sequence(assembly, chrom, start, end, strand=).

params.assembly: Genome assembly: hg38 (=GRCh38) or hg19 (=GRCh37). Never lifted over.
params.chrom: Chromosome, UCSC style (chr17, chrX, chrM); '17'/'X'/'MT' are accepted.
params.start: 0-based start (first base minus one). 1-based position P is start=P-1.
params.end: 0-based exclusive end (= the 1-based last base). Must be > start.
params.strand: '+' for the reference strand (default), '-' for reverse complement.

name: ucsc_get_region_annotations
description: Return records of one allowlisted UCSC track overlapping a window [start, end) on an explicit assembly: repeats (rmsk, simpleRepeat), segmental duplications (genomicSuperDups), problematic regions (encBlacklist, grcExclusions, GIAB difficult/low-mappability), phyloP, ENCODE cCREs, CpG islands, MANE/GENCODE/RefSeq transcripts, SpliceVarDB/Varaico variants. An empty problematic-region result means the window is not flagged. Native UCSC fields are kept and each record gains a normalized `position`; transcripts also gain `exons` numbered in transcript order (strand-aware), segmental duplications an `other_position` for the partner copy. `total` is exact (null only past the upstream item cap); `truncated` is honest. Windows: <= 2,000,000 bp, signal tracks <= 5,000 bp. Signature: get_region_annotations(assembly, chrom, start, end, track, limit=).

params.assembly: Genome assembly: hg38 (=GRCh38) or hg19 (=GRCh37). Never lifted over.
params.chrom: Chromosome, UCSC style (chr17, chrX, chrM); '17'/'X'/'MT' are accepted.
params.start: 0-based start (first base minus one). 1-based position P is start=P-1.
params.end: 0-based exclusive end (= the 1-based last base). Must be > start.
params.track: UCSC track name from list_tracks. phyloP is phyloP100way on hg38 and phyloP100wayAll on hg19 (either name works on both); cCREregistry/encodeCcreCombined/spliceVarDb are hg38-only.

name: ucsc_get_server_capabilities
description: Describe this server: allowlisted UCSC tracks per assembly with attribution and terms, coordinate convention, limits, rate-limit policy and error codes. Signature: get_server_capabilities().

name: ucsc_list_tracks
description: List the curated UCSC tracks this server can query, with the assemblies each exists on, window limits, provider attribution and terms of use (non_commercial flags SpliceVarDB and Varaico). Signature: list_tracks(assembly=).

params.assembly: Only tracks available on this assembly (default: all).

name: ucsc_predict_pcr_products
description: Predict every genomic product a primer pair amplifies up to max_product_size (in-silico PCR, as UCSC In-Silico PCR). Each product: location (0-based half-open + 1-based display), size, strand, per-primer mismatch counts and the product sequence (first 1,000 bp; primers uppercase). primary_total counts products off alt/fix contigs (alt_or_patch=true repeats a primary locus): primary_total == 1 is a single genomic product, 0 none. Primers need >= 15 perfect 3' bases. Runs on this deployment's own UCSC gfServer; an assembly that is not deployed answers upstream_unavailable (get_diagnostics -> blat shows what is live). Signature: predict_pcr_products(forward_primer, reverse_primer, assembly=, max_product_size=, limit=).

params.assembly: Genome assembly (default hg38). Never lifted over.

name: ucsc_search_genome
description: Find where a gene or transcript lies on an assembly (UCSC position search over MANE, HGNC, GENCODE and RefSeq). Returns 0-based half-open start/end plus a 1-based display string, ready for get_region_annotations. Exact symbol/accession hits come first (`exact_matches` counts them, each hit has `exact`), then UCSC's looser text matches on gene descriptions, which are weak: a disease name is not a gene lookup (resolve it with mondo_resolve_disease). UCSC search gives no strand: get_region_annotations(track='ncbiRefSeqSelect') does. Signature: search_genome(assembly, query, limit=).

params.assembly: Genome assembly: hg38 (=GRCh38) or hg19 (=GRCh37). Never lifted over.
params.query: Gene symbol, transcript accession or term, e.g. BRCA1, SHH, NM_007294.4, ENST00000357654.9.

name: uniprot_find_proteins
description: Search UniProtKB for the entries of a GENE and return matching entries (accession, mnemonic, recommended name, reviewed flag, organism). gene_symbol is REQUIRED; refine the hits with organism_taxon (a positive NCBI taxon id or an exact common/scientific organism name), reviewed, name_contains (matched per word, in any order, case-insensitive), or the structured filters mnemonic / ec_number / keyword. Reviewed (Swiss-Prot) hits are ranked first. UniProt SPARQL has no general full-text index; for EC-only, keyword-only, or free-text search WITHOUT a gene, use search_example_queries or search_sparql_query. Pair with get_protein for full detail. Results are ordered reviewed-first, then by mnemonic, then accession (stable across pages). Cold search can take several seconds; an identical repeat is cached (~0 ms). If you already know the accession, call get_protein directly -- it is far faster. Signature: find_proteins(gene_symbol, organism_taxon=, reviewed=, keyword=, ec_number=, mnemonic=, name_contains=, limit=, offset=).

params.gene_symbol: Gene symbol to search for, e.g. BRCA1.
params.organism_taxon: Positive NCBI taxon id or exact common/scientific organism name, e.g. 9606, 'human', or 'Homo sapiens'.
params.reviewed: True = Swiss-Prot only; False = TrEMBL only.
params.keyword: UniProt keyword (KW-id like KW-0007, or a label).
params.name_contains: Words to match in the recommended protein name. Multi-word input matches per word (each word must appear, in any order), so 'polynucleotide kinase' matches 'Bifunctional polynucleotide phosphatase/kinase'. Case-insensitive.
params.offset: Pagination offset.

name: uniprot_find_proteins_batch
description: Resolve SEVERAL gene symbols to UniProtKB entries in ONE call, running the lookups concurrently -- so N genes cost about one cold round-trip instead of N sequential ones. Use this for multi-gene tasks (e.g. 'get domains for PNKP and NAA10'). Returns by_gene (gene -> accessions, reviewed-first), a flat proteins list tagged with matched_gene, resolved_genes, and unresolved_genes (a symbol that matched nothing is disclosed, never silently dropped). Optionally scope by organism_taxon (a positive NCBI taxon id or an exact common/scientific organism name) and reviewed. next_commands fan out to get_protein on each resolved gene's top hit. For a single gene use find_proteins. Signature: find_proteins_batch(gene_symbols, organism_taxon=, reviewed=, limit_per_gene=).

params.organism_taxon: Positive NCBI taxon id or exact common/scientific organism name, e.g. 9606, 'human', or 'Homo sapiens'.
params.reviewed: True = Swiss-Prot only; False = TrEMBL only.

name: uniprot_get_example_query
description: Fetch one curated example's full SPARQL text, description, keyword tags, and any federated endpoints it joins. Pass an example_id (full IRI) from search_example_queries. `_meta.next_commands` offers to run it directly via search_sparql_query. Signature: get_example_query(example_id).

name: uniprot_get_protein
description: Return the core summary for a single UniProtKB entry by accession: mnemonic, reviewed flag, recommended/short name, gene(s), organism + taxon, protein existence, sequence length and mass, a function summary, and creation/modification dates, plus has_variants/has_diseases/has_structure presence flags that drive content-aware next_commands. An obsolete/demerged accession returns a flagged obsolete record (obsolete:true + replaced_by). response_mode (default compact) controls verbosity; standard/full add the created/modified dates. Signature: get_protein(accession, response_mode=).

params.accession: UniProtKB accession, e.g. P05067 (isoforms like P05067-2 accepted), or a human gene symbol, e.g. TP53 (resolved to its reviewed entry; see resolved_from).

name: uniprot_get_protein_cross_references
description: Return database cross-references for an entry, grouped by database (PDB, AlphaFoldDB, Ensembl, RefSeq, Reactome, STRING, InterPro, ...). Optionally restrict to specific databases (case-sensitive); any requested name that matched nothing is echoed under unmatched_databases with a did-you-mean, so a typo never reads as 'no data'. response_mode (default compact) returns short ids; full restores raw IRIs. Returns every cross-reference database; use resolve_identifiers for a focused primary-id mapping. Signature: get_protein_cross_references(accession, databases=, response_mode=).

params.accession: UniProtKB accession, e.g. P05067 (isoforms like P05067-2 accepted), or a human gene symbol, e.g. TP53 (resolved to its reviewed entry; see resolved_from).
params.databases: Database short names to keep (case-sensitive; omit for all). A malformed name is rejected (invalid_input); a well-formed name that matched nothing is echoed under unmatched_databases.

name: uniprot_get_protein_diseases
description: Return disease annotations associated with an entry: disease name, UniProt disease id, mnemonic, MIM id, the clinical `definition` (the disease vocabulary's own description), and `involvement` (the entry-specific note). Pairs with get_protein_variants for variant-level disease evidence. response_mode=compact/minimal drops the free-text definition/involvement; standard (default) preserves them. Signature: get_protein_diseases(accession, response_mode=).

params.accession: UniProtKB accession, e.g. P05067 (isoforms like P05067-2 accepted), or a human gene symbol, e.g. TP53 (resolved to its reviewed entry; see resolved_from).

name: uniprot_get_protein_features
description: Return sequence features with begin/end coordinates (FALDO) for an entry: domains, regions, transmembrane segments, binding/active sites, PTMs, signal peptides, secondary structure, mutagenesis sites, and more. feature_types=['domain'] returns curated positional domain extents; signature-database domains/families (InterPro/Pfam) are cross-references, pointed to by signature_domain_hint when no domain feature exists. Each returned `type` round-trips to the filter vocabulary. Filter keys come from capabilities (feature_types); a zero-match filter echoes the accepted keys as a filter_hint. Secondary-structure features (helix/strand/turn) are hidden by default and disclosed under excluded_secondary_structure; set include_secondary_structure=true (or name them in feature_types) to return them. DNA-binding extents are not available from UniProt RDF, so dna_binding is deliberately not a filter. response_mode=compact/minimal drops repeated fenced descriptions; standard (default) preserves existing full records. Signature: get_protein_features(accession, feature_types=, limit=, include_secondary_structure=, response_mode=).

params.accession: UniProtKB accession, e.g. P05067 (isoforms like P05067-2 accepted), or a human gene symbol, e.g. TP53 (resolved to its reviewed entry; see resolved_from).
params.feature_types: Feature-type keys to keep (omit for all). Closed vocabulary: an unrecognised key is rejected (invalid_input), never matched to nothing. See feature_types in get_server_capabilities.

name: uniprot_get_protein_go_terms
description: Return Gene Ontology annotations for an entry, grouped by aspect (biological_process / molecular_function / cellular_component) where available, each with GO id, label, and (when annotated) ECO `evidence` ids plus mapped GO `evidence_codes` (IDA/IEA/IMP/...) for citation. Always returns `count` and `count_by_aspect`; pass `aspect` to scope to one ontology and `limit` to cap a large set (token economy). Signature: get_protein_go_terms(accession, aspect=, limit=).

params.accession: UniProtKB accession, e.g. P05067 (isoforms like P05067-2 accepted), or a human gene symbol, e.g. TP53 (resolved to its reviewed entry; see resolved_from).
params.aspect: Restrict to one GO aspect (omit for all).

name: uniprot_get_protein_sequence
description: Return the amino-acid sequence(s) for an entry: the canonical isoform (length, mass, sequence) plus any additional (non-canonical) isoforms. Pass a canonical accession for all isoforms, or an isoform accession (e.g. P05067-2) to get THAT isoform's specific sequence and mass. response_mode controls verbosity: minimal=metadata only; compact (default)=length/mass + a first/last-30-residue sequence_preview (sequence_truncated:true) — cheap for large proteins; standard/full return the complete sequence string. Set canonical_only=true to return only the canonical isoform (skip the additional-isoform list). Signature: get_protein_sequence(accession, response_mode=, canonical_only=).

params.accession: UniProtKB accession, e.g. P05067 (isoforms like P05067-2 accepted), or a human gene symbol, e.g. TP53 (resolved to its reviewed entry; see resolved_from).
params.canonical_only: Return only the canonical isoform (omit the additional-isoform list).

name: uniprot_get_protein_variants
description: Return natural-variant annotations for an entry: position, wild-type residue, amino-acid substitution, an HGVS-style `notation` (e.g. `L176F`) for simple substitutions, `variant_type` (substitution|other), free-text description, structured linked `diseases`, and `dbsnp` rsIDs. Set disease_associated_only=true to keep only disease-linked variants. Set position_start and/or position_end to keep annotations that overlap that residue interval (inclusive). response_mode=compact/minimal drops the repeated free-text provenance; standard (default) preserves the existing full records. Signature: get_protein_variants(accession, limit=, disease_associated_only=, response_mode=, position_start=, position_end=).

params.accession: UniProtKB accession, e.g. P05067 (isoforms like P05067-2 accepted), or a human gene symbol, e.g. TP53 (resolved to its reviewed entry; see resolved_from).
params.disease_associated_only: Return only variants linked to a disease.
params.position_start: First residue of an inclusive overlap interval.
params.position_end: Last residue of an inclusive overlap interval.

name: uniprot_get_server_capabilities
description: Return the uniprot-link discovery surface. detail='summary' (default) is light: identity/build/release, the tool list WITH call signatures, accepted argument aliases, response modes, recommended workflows, error taxonomy, and limits -- enough to call any tool without guessing an argument name. detail='full' adds the heavy reference blocks (21 named graphs with triple counts, the full SPARQL prefix map, full latency bands, feature-type and cross-reference vocabularies). Call this first in a cold session, or read uniprot://tools (signatures only) or uniprot://capabilities (full). Signature: get_server_capabilities(detail=).

params.detail: summary (default, light) or full (adds named graphs/prefixes).

name: uniprot_get_taxon
description: Resolve an organism in the UniProt taxonomy. Pass a numeric NCBI taxon id (e.g. 9606) for full detail (scientific/common name, rank, the DIRECT parent, and an optional ordered lineage from species up to root), or a scientific/common name to get candidate taxon ids. Use the resolved taxon id with find_proteins(gene_symbol=..., organism_taxon=...). Name matches are ranked best-first (an exact scientific/common-name hit leads, tagged match_quality:'exact'), so matches[0] and next_commands point at the right organism. Numeric-id and common-organism-name lookups are fast (~0 ms for common names); an uncommon name triggers a multi-second taxonomy scan. Signature: get_taxon(taxon, include_lineage=).

params.taxon: NCBI taxon id (digits) or a scientific/common name.
params.include_lineage: Include the ancestor lineage (id lookups only).

name: uniprot_resolve_identifiers
description: Resolve a UniProtKB accession to its PRIMARY external identifiers: the genomic/structural/family core (PDB, AlphaFoldDB, Ensembl, RefSeq, GeneID, HGNC, KEGG, OrthoDB, Pfam, InterPro) by default. Optionally restrict to specific databases. Returns ids grouped by database plus the databases that matched and per-database counts. response_mode (default compact) returns short ids; full restores raw IRIs. For the exhaustive cross-reference set (incl. drug/disease databases like DrugBank/ChEMBL/OpenTargets) use get_protein_cross_references instead. Signature: resolve_identifiers(accession, databases=, response_mode=).

params.accession: UniProtKB accession, e.g. P05067 (isoforms like P05067-2 accepted), or a human gene symbol, e.g. TP53 (resolved to its reviewed entry; see resolved_from).
params.databases: Target database short names (case-sensitive; omit for the primary set).

name: uniprot_search_example_queries
description: Search UniProt's 126 curated, executable SPARQL example queries by free text over their descriptions and keyword tags (e.g. 'disease', '3D structure', 'cross-reference', 'taxonomy'). Returns example ids, descriptions, tags, and query types. Fetch the full query text with get_example_query, then run it via search_sparql_query. The best way to learn how to query UniProt. Signature: search_example_queries(text=, limit=).

params.text: Free-text filter over descriptions and keywords.

name: uniprot_search_sparql_query
description: Run a bounded SPARQL SELECT/ASK query against the UniProt endpoint; returns SELECT results as columns+rows JSON, ASK as a boolean. SERVICE federation and graph-returning CONSTRUCT/DESCRIBE forms are rejected. A LIMIT is auto-injected into unbounded SELECTs (see `_meta`/`truncated`). This is the escape hatch for anything the typed tools do not cover -- seed queries from search_example_queries. Use uniprot://prefixes for the standard PREFIX block. Broad, unanchored queries can take 10-60 s; bound lookups (anchored on an accession/gene/taxon) return in <2 s. Signature: search_sparql_query(query, result_format=, limit=, timeout_seconds=).

params.query: A complete SPARQL 1.1 query string. SELECT/ASK only; SERVICE federation and CONSTRUCT/DESCRIBE are rejected. An unbounded SELECT gets an auto-injected LIMIT.
params.result_format: Result serialisation. Use json for SELECT/ASK.
params.limit: LIMIT to inject when a SELECT lacks one (capped at 10000).

name: vep_annotate_variant
description: Use this for the full VEP annotation of one variant: consequences, gene/transcript impact, HGVS, MANE/canonical flags, SIFT/PolyPhen, plus variant-level CADD/GERP under position_scores and per-transcript REVEL/AlphaMissense, and gnomAD frequencies. Input is parsed, recoded if needed, sent to the VEP region endpoint, then shaped to response_mode (start compact; widen to standard/full only if needed). The standard tier filters noisy neighbour transcripts by default (set transcripts='all' for every isoform). Carries a provenance block (endpoint + citation) and _meta.next_commands follow-ups.

params.variant: A single variant (coordinate, rsID, HGVS, SPDI, or CNV) to annotate with the Ensembl Variant Effect Predictor.
params.assembly: Reference build for annotation. GRCh38 default.
params.response_mode: Verbosity tier: minimal (identity only), compact (default; representative transcript + frequencies), standard (filtered transcripts), or full (raw-ish payload). Position scores (CADD/GERP) appear once under position_scores at all tiers above minimal.
params.transcripts: standard-tier only: 'auto' (default) drops uninformative MODIFIER neighbour transcripts, collapses identical-effect isoforms (equivalent_transcript_ids), and caps to the most severe; 'all' returns every transcript uncollapsed. Each variant carries its own transcripts_summary {shown,collapsed,total} when filtered.
params.allele: Optional ALT filter for a multi-allelic input: an ALT base (e.g. 'A') or a full CHR-POS-REF-ALT. Omit to annotate every ALT allele (each as an entry in variants[]).
params.vep_options: Optional VEP flag overrides (keys must be in the allowlist; call get_capabilities for the set). Plugins like SpliceAI / dbNSFP are instance-dependent.

name: vep_annotate_variants_batch
description: Use this to annotate many variants (cap 200) in one call instead of looping annotate_variant. Returns a results list (each shaped to response_mode and tagged with its original input; a multi-allelic input such as rs6025 yields one result per ALT allele), a per-input errors list (parse/not-found failures that did not fail the batch), and a summary (requested/annotated/failed count inputs; result_rows counts result rows). Inputs still unresolved at the batch deadline (default 48 s) come back as per-input upstream_timeout errors next to the finished results; retry those alone. Each result's standard-tier transcript list is filtered by default; per-result truncation is reported in that result's transcripts_summary.

params.variants: Up to 200 variants to annotate in one call. Repeated inputs are annotated once; one bad or slow variant never fails the batch (its error is collected per-input).
params.assembly: Reference build for annotation. GRCh38 default.
params.response_mode: Verbosity tier applied to every result (default compact).
params.transcripts: standard-tier only: 'auto' (default) filters/caps each result's transcripts; 'all' returns every transcript. Each result carries its own transcripts_summary when truncated.
params.vep_options: Optional VEP flag overrides (keys must be in the allowlist).

name: vep_check_upstream_health
description: Use this to check whether the Ensembl REST hosts are healthy before a batch, or when calls start failing. Runs a live /info/ping of both assemblies (GRCh38 rest.ensembl.org, GRCh37 grch37.rest.ensembl.org) and returns each host's status (ok | recovering | down), circuit state, reachability, latency, and last error. If one build is degraded, route to the healthy one or back off. Returns <1kB.

name: vep_get_capabilities
description: Read this first in a cold session. Returns server/tool metadata: supported assemblies (GRCh38 default, GRCh37), input formats (coordinate, rsID, HGVS, SPDI, CNV), the VEP-option allowlist, the four response_mode tiers, the deterministic error codes, the citation contract, a capabilities_version hash a warm client can compare to skip re-fetching, and a live `upstream` health summary (per-assembly Ensembl REST status from the circuit breaker). No upstream call.

name: vep_liftover_variant
description: Use this to map a genomic coordinate (CHR-POS-REF-ALT) from one human assembly to the other (GRCh37 <-> GRCh38) via the Ensembl assembly-map endpoint. The two assemblies must differ. A unique mapping returns the lifted coordinate; zero mappings -> not_found, multiple -> ambiguous. HGVS/rsID inputs are unsupported (resolve_variant them first).

params.variant: A genomic coordinate (CHR-POS-REF-ALT) to lift between assemblies. HGVS/rsID are not liftable -- resolve them first.
params.from_assembly: Source assembly of the input coordinate.
params.to_assembly: Target assembly to lift the coordinate to (must differ from from_assembly).

name: vep_recode_variant
description: Use this to translate a variant (or a batch, cap 200) between identifier systems -- rsID <-> HGVS (g./c./p./t.) <-> VCF string <-> SPDI -- without a full VEP annotation. Returns one result object per input. Use the optional fields filter to trim the payload to just the representations you need.

params.variants: One or more variants (rsID, HGVS, coordinate, or SPDI) to recode into every equivalent representation. Cap 200.
params.assembly: Reference build for recoding. GRCh38 default.
params.fields: Optional comma-separated projection filter over the closed vocabulary vcf_string, hgvsg, hgvsc, hgvsp, spdi (e.g. 'hgvsg,spdi,vcf_string'); omit for the full set. An unknown field is rejected as invalid_input (it is not silently dropped).

name: vep_resolve_variant
description: Use this when the caller's variant is an rsID, HGVS, SPDI, or loosely formatted: returns a variants[] list (one entry per ALT allele) with the canonical CHR-POS-REF-ALT variant_id, gene_symbol and most_severe_consequence that the annotation tools build on, plus a top-level warnings[] (a multi-allelic input carries a multiple_alts warning). Coordinates are normalized locally; rsIDs/HGVS are recoded via Ensembl. Cheap (<1kB). Then call annotate_variant for the full VEP annotation.

params.variant: A variant in any supported form: CHR-POS-REF-ALT, an rsID (e.g. rs6025), genomic/transcript HGVS, or SPDI.
params.assembly: Reference build for resolution. GRCh38 default.
params.allele: Optional ALT filter for a multi-allelic input: an ALT base (e.g. 'A') or a full CHR-POS-REF-ALT. Omit to return every ALT allele in variants[].
